Risk read on GIGACHAD (class ORGANIC, alive, 30.5 min old):

- Pool depth is 130 SOL, roughly $25k+, so a $20 ticket is trivially small versus liquidity. Round-trip cost is near the low end of the range, about 1.4-2%.
- Volume is heavy (~$170k in 15 min) but net flow is only +68.6 SOL against 670 SOL sold, and sellers outnumber buyers. The 26% drawdown from the 30-min high and sell-to-buy ratio above 1 point to distribution, not accumulation.
- The first two minutes show a launch bot and a top-5 buyer share of 33%, which is worth caution.

If the desk buys: $5 ticket, 25% stop, 30-minute max hold.

I'd refuse any size if the drawdown deepens past the stop, if sells keep exceeding buys on the next check, or if bundled or top-holder share rises. Given the base rates and the sell pressure, I lean toward skipping.
memos.scout:
The strongest case for buying is the volume and breadth. In the last 15 minutes, 1,105 buyers put in 738 SOL against 670 SOL sold, and 328 buyers have touched the curve overall. Top-3 holder share is only 8.8%, and the curve's completer share (33%) and bundle share (30%) are high but not extreme. The coin is alive, up 146% over 30 minutes, and has pulled back only 26% from its high, which is a shallower dip than most collapsing memecoins show. Net flow was still positive (+68.6 SOL) in the latest window.

The case is weak, though. Sells are running at roughly 91% of buys, the 15-minute return is decaying, and a 30% bundle share plus a launch bot suggests some coordinated early activity. The pool is 130 SOL deep, so a $20 ticket will carry about 1.4-5% round-trip cost. Demand looks real for now, but nothing in the brief shows it will persist 30-60 minutes out, and the base rate for this stage is negative. I would not buy on this brief.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a post-pump distribution after a 1.8x run. In the last 15 minutes, sellers (773) nearly matched buyers (1105), and sell volume was 669.75 SOL against 738.32 SOL bought, so net flow was only 68.57 SOL. That is weak conviction at a high. The price is already 26% below its 30-minute high, which fits early holders taking profit. Launch-bot presence and a sell-to-buy ratio above 1 in the first two minutes after graduation (1.11) point to early exits too. Pool depth of 130 SOL means a $20 round trip faces roughly 3-5% in fees and impact, so a modest bounce gets eaten. Skip.
